the instruments.what: THE CITATIONS WATCH. Reads the library and grades every source — on every change to library/, on a :47 rung, and by hand. Fires on CHANGE rather than only on a clock, because the moment to ask where a text came from is while whoever added it still remembers. EMPTY fails the run; THIN and DATED report and do not, so a room whose translator is named and whose edition is not yet found is mid-work rather than broken.
the instruments.authority: LIVE. NO continue-on-error ANYWHERE, deliberately: on 24 Aug 2026 merge.js threw under it and the manifest froze for ninety hours behind a green tick. Its audit step tells a CRASH apart from a FINDING — exit 2 means the instrument did not run and says NOTHING BELOW IS A READING, exit 1 means a work has no source. The first draft used `|| echo empty=1`, which is the same blindness written small: it would have reported a missing LIBRARY.json as an empty citation. The readings are committed BEFORE the gate, so a red run still leaves a register behind.

the instruments.what: CITE A ROOM. Run from the Actions tab: give a room key and a citation, and it stamps every work in that room that has none, regenerates LIBRARY.json and CITATIONS.json, and commits. DRY RUN IS ON BY DEFAULT — the first run shows exactly what would change and writes nothing. With the source left blank it reports the gap and stops, which is the correct first run.
the instruments.authority: LIVE. IT EXISTS BECAUSE tools/cite.js WAS BUILT AS A COMMAND FOR A CAPTAIN WHO WORKS FROM GITHUB IN A BROWSER AND HAS NO TERMINAL TO TYPE IT INTO. A tool that cannot be reached by the person who needs it is not a tool; it is a file. Shares the `citations` concurrency lane with the citations watch so the two can never write LIBRARY.json over each other. Other rooms still holding empty sources do NOT fail this run — it stamped the room it was asked to stamp — but a crashed audit does.

the instruments.what: THE CITATION AUDIT. Reads LIBRARY.json and grades every work's source into four states — CITED (an edition that can be found again), DATED (a year, no identifier), THIN (a name with nothing to find it by), EMPTY — plus LINKED, which is not a fault. Says WHICH thing each room needs rather than only that something is wrong. First run, 29 Aug 2026: 405 cited, 77 empty, 52 thin — 11 rooms of 52.
the instruments.authority: LIVE. Exists because probe-library.mjs faithfully RECORDS what the manifests say and nothing READ what it recorded: 77 blank sources sat in the Lincoln room, on the most-quoted figure on the site, for as long as they were blank. AN EMPTY SOURCE STRING READS AS A FIELD RATHER THAN A GAP. EMPTY fails the run; THIN and DATED report and do not, so a gap somebody is working through cannot hold a workflow red for weeks. It is careful about what it refuses to call a fault — a link-out, a pointer to another shelf on this site, and the project's own published work are all correct citations, and its first draft flagged the last of those until it was taught otherwise. A RULE THAT FLAGS CORRECT WORK TEACHES THE READER TO IGNORE THE REPORT.

the instruments.what: THE POSTING GATE, 29 Aug 2026. Reads a queue of proposed social posts and REFUSES the ones that would put words in a real person's mouth. Exits non-zero, so a workflow can gate on it. Enforces: every quotation carries a source; the note is the SITE'S voice and not the figure's; no quoted speech smuggled into an unsourced field; the figure is on the roster; the post fits without truncation; and THE LIVING-MEMORY LINE at seventy years — a judgment, written in the file so it can be argued with.
the instruments.authority: LIVE, and HONEST ABOUT ITS LIMIT — there is no machine-readable corpus of what these figures wrote, so it CANNOT verify that a quotation is real. It refuses unsourced ones instead, which forces the citation to exist and makes a fabrication a deliberate act rather than an accident. IT FAILS CLOSED: no roster, nothing approved. Its rule is the daily rotation addendum's, applied where no reader is present to ask. Running it against the LIVE roster rather than a fixture found its own worst bug: Caesar's Death-Date is "-44" — the roster stores BC as a negative number, not as letters — so the first parser read it as the year 44 and would have held every pre-Christian figure in the cast as too recent to post.

the book itself.what: THE CONVERSATION DOCTRINE. The governing logic for two-way voice and text conversation between a seeker and a figure — the spec the chat core's state machine and system prompt are built from. Deliberately a doctrine and not a feature list, so every mount (Terminal, reading vault, Atlantica, news article) inherits one coherent character instead of four drifting ones. Its one line above all others: patient with humans, stingy with waste, never hang up on someone who is present or hurting. Extended 27 Aug 2026 with §4.6, WHAT THE FIGURE REMEMBERS: the figure never asks for more than a name, but may remember what it was told. Holds the coarseness rule that makes memory safe — a region never a town, a kind of work never an employer, no age and no surname, because many users are young — and the rule that recognition is in the answering, not in a recital.
the book itself.authority: canonical, and LIVE — this is a governing document, not an account of a day. If it and amenti-chat.js disagree, that is a finding.

the book itself.what: THE MANUAL, 29 Aug 2026. HOW TO USE AMENTI, written twice over: part one for somebody who has just arrived and wants to know what this is, part two for somebody already inside who wants to know what a particular room does. Covers all eleven doors, and gives THE FIVE MODES the space nothing on the site gives them — what to BRING to each, the adversary's yield rule and the witness's silence rule. Also states the things a reader cannot discover by clicking: that a figure answers honestly when asked what it is, that it will not recite your own words back, that it may send you to another figure, that nothing overheard is recorded, and what an hour costs.

the registers — read at the hour of writ.what: THE LIBRARY, READ. What reading rooms exist and which actually hold works — 52 rooms, 550 works, 31 MB of text, every one with its title, its section and ITS SOURCE. THIS IS THE CORPUS, and it was here all along: most works carry a full citation with translator, edition and Project Gutenberg number. Josephus has all 29 books; Shakespeare 45 works and the First Folio; Caesar both commentaries in McDevitte 1869. A room's `missing` array names manifest entries whose files are absent, and hasCard/hasTerminal say whether the room is wired to the rest of the site.
the registers — read at the hour of writ.authority: LIVE, and GENERATED by probes/probe-library.mjs — never hand-edited. Meaning and citations live in the per-figure manifests at library/{key}.json. THE READING IS ONLY AS HONEST AS THOSE MANIFESTS: on 29 Aug it faithfully reported 77 blank sources in the Lincoln room, which were not a mystery but one book's table of contents — Speeches and Letters of Abraham Lincoln 1832-1865, ed. Merwin Roe, PG #14721 — with the citation written once on the single work pulled into its own file and never propagated. Fixed with tools/cite.js. AN EMPTY SOURCE STRING READS AS A FIELD RATHER THAN A GAP, which is why it sat unnoticed on the most-quoted figure on the site.

the registers — read at the hour of writ.what: THE BOOK, MEASURED. Every chapter against BOOK.json: state, size, the bands it carries, the day it landed. Movements, totals and a timeline.

the registers — read at the hour of writ.what: WHAT ALREADY SERVES THIS. The register keyed by the QUESTION A BUILDER ASKS rather than by the file that answers it — 22 needs, each with what serves it, WHAT IT DOES NOT ANSWER, and a note. Opened 29 Aug 2026 after the same fault twice in one session: a corpus written while LIBRARY.json held 550 works, and a reader's manual written when an operator's map had been asked for. Every other register in this fleet is keyed by PATH, so learning whether a capability exists means reading 181 glosses and recognising one. Nobody does that, and things get built twice.
the registers — read at the hour of writ.authority: AUTHORED BY HAND, and READ AT THE TOP OF A BUILD. Its law: A CAPABILITY THAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE WILL BE BUILT AGAIN — not a threat, a description of what happened. `doesNotAnswer` is as load-bearing as `servedBy`: a register that says what it covers and not what it omits invites the second mistake, trusting it too far. Needs with servedBy null are the honest state, not a gap — a need written down and unbuilt is a need that will not be built twice.

the registers — read at the hour of writ.what: THE SOURCE INDEX. Every document the book draws on, with a path verified by raw HTTP status, and a drift report naming what is unreachable and what is unindexed. Read this first; walk from it to everything else.

THE CAPTAIN'S WINDOW ON THE FLEET. Reads fleet.json (intent) and fleet-dispatch.json (reality) live and lays them side by side: for each tube, what it is meant to do against what it actually fired. State-aware — a paused tube reading quiet is calm; a live tube that has never fired shows red. The map of the presses, self-reading, so the fleet can be read at a glance instead of interrogated.

The Harbor. The way in. Its pane grid is BUILT from window.FLEET_PANES in fleet-nav.js — hand-written until 28 Aug 2026, when it was found holding thirteen cards against a registry of eighteen, with two panes sharing the number Pane IV. the surfaces.what: THE READING DESK. The nineteenth pane. Every markdown document in the fleet, RENDERED — and printable to PDF through the browser's own dialog. It exists because eleven documents sat in the flagship's root and the only way to read one was a monospaced blob on GitHub. Filing them into docs/ was the other answer and was refused: three are FETCHED AT RUNTIME by their root path, and a tidy folder that breaks the hall is not tidy.
the surfaces.authority: LIVE, and A REFLECTION — it holds no list of its own. The shelf is built from SOURCES.json, so a document that acquires a sentence appears here and one nobody has described appears marked undescribed. Its markdown renderer is small and local by choice, and was found wrong by testing it against the REAL documents: bold that opened on one line and closed on the next survived as asterisks, because blockquote lines were formatted separately. A sample would never have caught it.

the surfaces.what: THE SURFACE MANIFEST. The eighteenth pane. Reads SURFACES.json and shows every place a person can act on this system, with four columns saying what reaches each: counted, memory, dial, voice. A checked-false renders as a dot and an UNCHECKED as a question mark, because false is a claim and null is an admission.
the surfaces.authority: LIVE. A reflection, generated at open, holding no list of its own — and it appears in the register it renders, because a map that omits itself is the fault it was built to catch.

the log.what: CAPTAIN'S LOG, 27–28 Aug 2026. What was built, what was FOUND, what is running, and what is still only claimed — across a session that shipped three ReferenceError fixes, figure memory end to end, the visit reading, prompt caching, voice priced and metered, and the surface register from brief to pane. §III holds the findings and §IV holds the assistant's own errors, because a log that records only the wins is a log nobody can trust the rest of. Also records the FOUR-DAY BLINDNESS: fleet-semantics.js overwritten with the source index on 24 Aug, hidden because merge.js threw a raw SyntaxError under continue-on-error while the gate announced a wiring bug that did not exist — and the correction that the commit which destroyed the Harbor in August was never foreign, but a Copilot-suggested message nobody read.
the log.authority: an ACCOUNT OF A DAY, not a governing document. Deploy states are the captain's confirmations, not the assistant's assumptions. Where this and a register disagree, the register is right.

the log.what: CAPTAIN'S LOG, 29–30 Aug 2026. A session that began with Abraham Lincoln speaking in a woman's voice and ended with every work in the library carrying a source. §I holds the findings — the roster never reaching the voice, the wildcard reset that swallowed four gutter fixes, four duplicate selectors in one night, the announcement and the greeting playing together, the Links column that cites nothing, and 77 of Lincoln's 82 works with no source. §III is the reading: 482 of 550 cited, EMPTY zero. §V is the assistant's own errors, and is the longest section.
the log.authority: an ACCOUNT OF A DAY, not a governing document. Its numbers were READ from CITATIONS.json at 06:56:42Z and are stamped with that hour. Where this and a register disagree, the register is right.

the log.what: THE HANDOFF, 30 Aug 2026. What the next session needs before it starts. Opens with the single most useful fact about this project and the one discovered latest: THE CAPTAIN WORKS FROM GITHUB IN A BROWSER AND HAS NO TERMINAL, so anything that must be run is a workflow and never a command. Says what belongs in the project folder and what must be kept out of it, the five things that will bite, the work in the order it will hurt to leave undone, and Hume's six Gutenberg numbers so they need never be found again.
the log.authority: a handoff, and STALE THE MOMENT A REGISTER MOVES. Read it at the top of a session and check anything load-bearing against the register it names. Replaces the previous handoff — two in one folder is the water between.

the slipway.what: THREE MOVES FOR THE STANDING SLIP, 28 Aug 2026 — Quote, Note and Quiz of the Day. Argues they are siblings of Person of the Day and should share ONE written register rather than four rotations that drift, and rules that the QUOTE MUST BE A CITATION INTO THE CORPUS and never generated: a fabricated quotation on the front page is the moat breached in the most quotable place on the site.
the slipway.authority: a slip addendum. Nothing built. Paste into THE STANDING SLIP and number there.

the slipway.what: THE EDITIONS STILL TO FIND, opened 30 Aug 2026. THE CITATION WORK IS DONE and this holds what is left of it: nine rooms that name a translator and stop short of the edition that would let a reader find the text again. 550 works, 495 cited, EMPTY zero — against 482 and 77 blanks the same morning. Carries the method that identified Lincoln’s and Hume’s editions (match the room’s titles, in their order, against a book’s table of contents), the whole cite-a-room procedure in three modes, and the three form-field traps met live.
the slipway.authority: LIVE, and NOT URGENT BY DESIGN. citations.yml fails the build on an EMPTY source and only reports THIN and DATED, because a room whose translator is named and whose edition is not yet found is mid-work rather than broken. Its acceptance test allows a ruling instead of a fix: Lincoln’s two, Shaka’s oral tradition and Milton’s unknown edition may be as good as they will get, AND THAT SHOULD BE WRITTEN DOWN rather than left to look like unfinished work.

the slipway.what: TWO MOVES, 28 Aug 2026. THE SECOND VOICE — two figures on one question, a scene not a room, because one-on-one is intense and intensity is a demand; the counsel already does most of it, so it is a change of STAGING not a new system. And THE WAY IN — a page asking what a reader wants rather than who they have heard of, with categories as TAGS on figures so the roster can surprise: nobody clicks Caesar to ask about religion, and he was Pontifex Maximus for twenty years. Also records why letters from figures were parked.
the slipway.authority: a slip addendum. Nothing built. The scene must be TESTED by hand before it is built — two dollars decides it. The categories are the captain’s to set.

the gameroom — found 19 Aug, on no list.what: The gameroom. Linked from Page1's nav as GAMEROOM.
The referee's message protocol — the contract the game client implements.

A Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object relaying chess moves over WebSockets. One instance per room code; authoritative on turn order, NOT on chess legality — the client validates that. Built on the WebSocket Hibernation API.

_finding: THE HUB LINKS EIGHT BRIEFS. THE REPO HOLDS FORTY-ONE. The Engineering tab shows a subset and does not say so, and this index was built from that tab — so its first cut was missing thirty-three documents, including the SPEECH DOCTRINE and THE SACRED FRAMES, which are the two capabilities the captain names as the ones that make the site what it is. A list that shows part of a thing without saying which part is the same fault as a green lamp with nothing behind it.
